title: Created a content engine for my game using Fable
author: nsjames1
selftext:
I'm starting to push on GTM for this game I've been working on, and wanted to set up a content engine so that I could churn out good content for platforms. Some design requirements:

* It must have short captivating hooks in the first 3-4 seconds of the video
* I want both gameplay and mechanics shorts
* I want subtitles for muted viewers
* I want to be able to "stage" scenes so that I can display mechanics
* I want to use Buffer to schedule posts to tiktok/instagram/youtube

  
I set fable off with a prompt that included all of those things (I went into much more depth there, and iterated a bunch). 

  
I iterated on a few early videos to get camera work, intriguing moments, voices, captions, and hook elements right. Took about 3 hours worth of back and forth to get the videos to something decent enough that I could then go to sleep and send it off to generate 20 videos. 

  
It works in 2 ways:

1. For mechanics videos, it uses staged scenes where I can tell the "bots"/players to do whatever I want, but using the real authoritative and client code from the game so there's no divergence between the capture and actual gameplay.
2. For gameplay videos, it has two teams of 10 bots each battling it out (I already had bot scripts with a "bot brain" that knows how the game works, and I'd been iterating that over the past 4-ish weeks), it does a couple of those matches, and then identifies key moments in the battles (high kills, heavy battles, killing sprees, stale mate battles, etc) and creates titles/scripts that match what happened in each of those snippets

I ended up using 11labs with a recording of my own voice to do the voiceovers. I hate how it made me sound (like some super excited influencer person), but I realized it's probably the best intonation/emotion that could be used for these types of videos. 

For Buffer, I'm using the API to be able to push videos from my local to their scheduling service, which requires that those videos are hosted somewhere, so I threw up a bucket and placed the videos with a TTL that culls them after their posting date. 

I think I might take it an extra step in the future and have it use the typical bottom-placed human reaction video, though I don't know if I'll use meme reactions or ai generated reactions of myself so that I can control copyrights/permissive use.

Overall I think the system works pretty well, but since I just posted the first few videos I'll come back with the results in a few weeks and a post-mortem analysis of what worked and what didn't. 

Ideally I would have open sourced this, but a lot of it relies on unity code that is directly dependent on my specific game, so here's an output from Claude by asking it to create a prompt to give another agent to recreate this. 



    Build me an automated short-form video pipeline for my game, for TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels.
    
    Footage: record real matches through the game's actual server with bots, never a mocked or re-simulated version, so what's on screen always matches the real game rules. Run a capture client as a normal bot, kept out of the shipping build. For mechanics videos, stage short scenes with scripted bots pressing real inputs. Never change game code just for the videos.
    
    Format: vertical 1080x1920. The full game view on top, a bar with the website URL in the middle (the call to action), and a close-up below that follows the action and frames each kill. Never put text over the top panel.
    
    Two kinds of video:
    1. Gameplay shorts: open cold on a fight with the hook spoken in the first second. Cut only around the player's kills and drop every lull, keeping it 7 to 20 seconds.
    2. Mechanics videos: about 6 seconds each, one ability per video, showing it clearly doing its job.
    
    Voice: generate voiceover in my cloned voice, with a different emotion and pace on every video, never one shared template. Transcribe the voice for word timings, so key words land on the moment they describe. Show the spoken words as bold, animated one-word captions near the bottom. Keep game sound under the voice.
    
    Hooks: each opens a real curiosity gap and claims only what the footage and server logs prove. No "POV:", no "wait for it".
    
    Checks: check every render automatically for frozen frames, black frames, missing sound and layout, and verify claims against the server log. Show me 2 or 3 videos per round, not dozens.
    
    Publishing: build a local web page that lists every video with its status, and a one-click "add to queue" that uploads the video to a storage bucket and schedules it to every network through Buffer's API. Delete each upload automatically a day after its last post.
